newsitem.title: CHINA: China power market seen growing 10 pct per year.
newsitem.headline: China power market seen growing 10 pct per year.

text.p: China's electric power market is seen growing by up to 10 percent a year, with much of the growth coming from foreign energy firms, the China Daily newspaper said on Friday.
China's installed electricity generation capacity was at 210,000 megawatts by 1995 and that was expected to grow to between 270,000-300,000 megawatts by the year 2000, the newspaper said.
"Forty percent of the additional power capacity will depend on imported equipment," it quoted an official of the Ministry of Machinery Industry as saying.
The State Planning Commission was drafting new rules aimed at regulating foreign investment in China, the newspaper said without elaborating.

China was planning to build four new nuclear power stations in the next five years, it said, adding that Japanese firms Hitachi and Toshiba would offer tenders to sell China reactors for the projects. It gave no further details.
